answer: Colours by mode. CSS: comments, selectors, properties, values, numbers, strings. JavaScript: keywords rgb(119, 0, 136), names being defined rgb(0, 0, 255), methods rgb(0, 0, 204), classes rgb(17, 102, 119), strings rgb(170, 17, 17), templates and regexes rgb(238, 68, 0), numbers rgb(17, 102, 68), atoms rgb(34, 17, 153), comments rgb(153, 68, 0). Plain Text none. CSS, JavaScript and Plain Text don't wrap; HTML and Markdown do. HTML mode marks by the caret: after < or at a tag's end that tag's two bracket tokens, after the name the name in both tags. The reads skip to the second cm-content: what comes first is the panel behind the view. The JavaScript read stopped at 80 elements, so let, undefined and export default are unread and ours is inferred. In the CSS read a { color: red } showed odd green punctuation: unexplained, unread.
